segments: Welcome back, in this video I will discuss multi-class support vector machine.
This is one of the important concepts in machine learning and data analytics.
Support vector machine is used to solve classification and regression task.
The basic SVM algorithm is designed for binary classification.
It means that it separates data into two classes using hyperplane.
In this graph, we can see that we have two classes, one class is represented with red
color and one more class is represented with green color and these two classes are separated
by hyperplane.
But in the real world problem, the classes may be more than two, such as if you go for
classifying the emails, we will get the mails like a genuine spam, promotion, social and
updates mails and if you go for classifying the images, we get the different images like
a cat, dog, horse or a bird images and if you go for classifying the diseases, we will
get a number of diseases like diabetes, heart attack and cancer.
All these three problems are having more than two classes and in this graph also we can
see that here we have three classes and to separate these three classes, we cannot do
it from the support vector machine because for separation of these classes, we need multiple
hyperplanes.
So, to solve this problem, we need to use multi-class support vector machine.
So, this vector machine allows classification among three or more classes.
Multi-class SVM, it is an extension of SVM algorithm used to classify data into more
than two classes by combining multiple binary classifiers.
There are several strategies to implement multi-class classification using SVM.
Those are one versus rest and one versus one.
So, first we will understand one versus rest method.
In one versus rest, we train one classifier for each class.
It means that if k classes are there, we train k binary classifiers.
To understand this method, we will take one simple example.
In this, we need to classify fruits.
Here we have three classes like orange, apple and banana.
In the first step of one versus rest method, we need to build a classifier.
As I already told, in this method, if k number of classes are there, we need to build k classifiers.
So, here we have three classes, we will get three classifiers.
Those are SVM 1, SVM 2 and SVM 3.
So, in the SVM 1, apple will be taken as a positive class and banana and orange will
be taken as a negative class.
And in SVM 2, banana will be taken as a positive class, apple and orange will be taken as a
negative class.
And in SVM 3, orange will be taken as a positive class and apple and banana will be taken as
a negative class.
In the next step, we need to predict the label for new example.
That new example will be given as a input for these classifiers.
So, these classifiers will predict the prediction score.
So, the prediction scores will look something like this.
It means that SVM 1 will predicted as 0.7, SVM 2 as a 0.9, SVM 3 as a 0.3.
So, in this course, 0.9 is a maximum value, this is from the SVM 2.
It means we need to consider SVM 2 classifier and in a SVM 2 classifier, banana is a positive
class.
It means that the new example will be predicted as banana.
Now, we will discuss advantage and disadvantage of one versus rest method.
So, advantages are easy to implement.
It requires only K classifier.
It means if you have K classes, we will get K classifiers.
So, disadvantages, class imbalance may occur.
It means that here we can see, in this case, we have three classes and in each class, if
you take a 10 examples, so for SVM 1, in the positive class, we will get only 10 examples
and in the negative class, we will get a 20 examples.
So, this will create the imbalance.
So, this is the one of the disadvantage of one versus rest method.
So, next we will go for one versus one method.
In one versus one, a classifier is trained for every pair of classes.
It means if you have K classes, the number of classifier will be K into K minus 1 divided
by 2.
To understand this one, we will take one simple example.
So, here we need to classify the fruits.
In this, we have three classes, apple, banana and orange.
First step, we need to build the classifier.
As I already told, in the one versus one classifier, the classifiers will be K into K minus 1 divided
by 2, where K is the number of classes.
So, here the number of classes are three.
So, 3 into 3 minus 1 divided by 2, which is equal to 3.
So, we will get a three classes like SVM 1, SVM 2 and SVM 3.
So, in SVM 1, we will take a classes as apple and banana.
In SVM 2, we will take a classes as apple and orange.
In SVM 3, we will take a classes as banana and orange.
So, once the training is done, the next step is to predict the class label for new example.
And that new example is given as input to these classifiers.
And these classifiers will predict one of the class for that particular new example.
So, here we can see that SVM 1 is predicted as an apple, SVM 2 is predicted as an orange,
SVM 3 is predicted as an orange.
After that, we need to find the vote for each and every class.
Here, we can see that for the class apple, the vote is 1 because from SVM 1 only, it is predicted
as an apple.
And for orange, we will get two votes that is from SVM 2 and SVM 3.
And banana is 0.
And here, we can see that the class orange is having highest vote that is 2.
It means that the new example is predicted as orange.
So, next one is advantages of one versus one method.
So, one versus one method is more accurate, works well for small data sets.
And disadvantage is many classifiers required.
It means that as the number of classes increases, exponentially the number of classifiers will
increase.
So, here we can see that if the classes are 3, we will get the classifiers as 3.
But if the classes are 10, in that case, 10 into 10 minus 1 divided by 2, which is equal to 45.
It means we will get a 45 classifiers for the 10 classes.
So, this is one of the disadvantage of one versus one method.
This is how we implement multiclass support vector machine.
I hope the concept is clear.
